read_file.description: Read a UTF-8 file before inspecting or changing its contents. The returned lines are numbered from one. Optional start_line and end_line select an inclusive range; omitted or null bounds select the corresponding file boundary.

path.description: File path to inspect; use the exact project path you need to understand before editing.

start_line.description: First 1-based line to return; use null to start at the beginning of the file.

end_line.description: Last 1-based line to return; use null to read through the end of the file.

content.description: Selected UTF-8 lines with their original one-based line numbers.

write_file.description: Create a UTF-8 file or replace its complete contents, creating parent directories when necessary. Provide the complete desired text; use edit_file for a change limited to an existing line range.

path.description: Destination file path to create or fully replace.

content.description: Complete UTF-8 contents the destination file must contain after the write.

written.description: True when the complete file was written successfully; otherwise the requested write did not complete.

edit_file.description: Replace an inclusive, one-based line range in an existing UTF-8 file. Obtain current line numbers with read_file before editing. Both range bounds are required integers; an invalid range fails without changing the file.

path.description: Existing file path whose selected lines should be replaced.

start_line.description: Required integer: first one-based line of the inclusive range to replace.

end_line.description: Required integer: last one-based line of the inclusive range to replace.

content.description: Complete replacement text for the selected line range.

edited.description: True when the requested range was replaced successfully; false means the file was not changed as requested.

execute_command.description: Execute one non-interactive bash command with an optional working directory. Shell composition belongs in command. Execution has no result timeout; use exit_code, stdout and stderr to assess the completed operation. Deleting the calling agent cancels its command and child processes.

command.description: One complete non-interactive bash command to run; include all required arguments and shell composition here.

cwd.description: Working directory; omitted or null uses the project root.

exit_code.description: Process exit code; use it with stdout and stderr to determine whether the command succeeded.

stdout.description: Captured standard output produced by the command; inspect it for requested results, diagnostics, or test output.

stderr.description: Captured standard error produced by the command; inspect it for failures, warnings, and diagnostics.

memory_write.description: Write a message from your past self to your future self in semantic memory. Record one confirmed, self-contained fact likely to remain true in the near future: a person's stable habits, character, preferences, interests, biography or relationships, or persistent information about devices and surroundings. State the established fact directly, with enough context to understand it later. Do not record uncertain inferences, hypothetical possibilities, plans as completed events, current tasks, temporary projects or short-lived states. Do not infer a habit from one observation or duplicate an existing entry, PERSON or ENVIRONMENT. The core generates the entry ID.

content.description: One short, self-contained message to your future self stating a confirmed fact expected to remain stable in the near future. Include whom or what the fact concerns; exclude uncertainty, hypothetical plans, current tasks and temporary states.

id.description: Generated ID of the saved semantic memory entry; use the ID currently shown in MEMORY for later editing or deletion.

memory_edit.description: Replace the complete text of an existing semantic memory entry by its ID. Write a clear message to your future self containing the corrected, confirmed and sufficiently stable fact. Preserve relevant established information; do not turn possibilities, intentions or uncertain conclusions into facts.

id.description: Exact ID of the existing MEMORY entry to replace.

content.description: Complete replacement message to your future self, stating the corrected confirmed and stable information clearly enough to understand without the current conversation.

status.description: Operation result; updated means the identified memory entry was replaced.

memory_delete.description: Delete a semantic memory entry by its ID when its information is false, obsolete, duplicated or no longer suitable as a confirmed stable message to your future self.

id.description: Exact ID of the MEMORY entry that should be removed permanently.

status.description: Operation result; deleted means the identified memory entry was removed.

reply.description: Send the exact text to the human interlocutor through the console response channel. This capability is offered when voice output is unavailable because the configured speech executable is absent. The text appears inside the protocol trace.

text.description: Exact user-facing text to return through the fallback console response.

status.description: Operation result; successful means the fallback reply was emitted.

create_preset.description: Create a reusable agent specialization before creating its live instances. Provide a personality and purpose together with appropriate initial capability IDs; personality text contains identity, character and professional knowledge, not execution instructions or delegation rules. Prefer a matching existing preset over duplicating it. The built-in module_manager specialization is exclusively for creating capabilities: using it for any other task is forbidden. The new preset affects only future instances.

preset_id.description: Stable short identifier for the new preset; choose a name that identifies the intended agent type, not one temporary task instance.

person_prompt.description: Identity, personality, purpose and relevant professional knowledge of future instances. Keep operational instructions, capability selection and delegation rules out of this text.

actions.description: Standalone action IDs that every new instance of this preset should have; assign only actions appropriate to the preset purpose.

handlers.description: Handler IDs that every new instance of this preset should observe; assign only event sources needed for the preset purpose.

modules.description: Module IDs whose bundled capabilities every new instance of this preset should receive; use whole modules rather than listing their members separately.

status.description: Creation result; created means the preset now exists, not_created means it was not created.

preset_id.description: Identifier of the preset whose creation was attempted.

error.description: Reason preset creation failed when status is not_created; use it to correct the definition before retrying.

edit_preset.description: Replace an existing preset's complete personality and initial capability assignments for future instances. Describe identity, character, purpose and professional knowledge in PERSON; capability usage belongs in capability descriptions. Existing instances keep their current personality, context and assignments.

preset_id.description: Identifier of the existing preset whose future definition should be replaced.

person_prompt.description: Complete replacement identity, personality, purpose and relevant professional knowledge for future instances, without task execution or delegation instructions.

actions.description: Complete set of standalone action IDs future instances of this preset should receive.

handlers.description: Complete set of handler IDs future instances of this preset should observe.

modules.description: Complete set of module IDs future instances of this preset should receive as bundled capabilities.

status.description: Edit result; edited means the preset definition was replaced, not_edited means it was left unchanged.

preset_id.description: Identifier of the preset whose edit was attempted.

error.description: Reason the preset edit failed when status is not_edited; use it to correct the replacement definition.

remove_preset.description: Remove a preset together with its agent instances and their descendants when that specialization is no longer needed. Their execution resources and persisted instance information are removed. Use delete_agent when only one instance should be removed. Protected presets cannot be removed.

preset_id.description: Identifier of the preset to remove together with all of its live instances and descendants.

status.description: Removal result; removed means the preset and affected instance tree were removed, not_removed means they were not.

preset_id.description: Identifier of the preset whose removal was attempted.

error.description: Reason removal failed when status is not_removed; inspect it before deciding whether to retry.

create_automation.description: Save an exact event-to-action rule for a fixed reaction that does not require new model reasoning. Provide exactly one event or call_result trigger and a non-empty actions array without call_id. The entire trigger structure and data must match; only the call_result trigger's call_id value is ignored. Each triggered invocation receives a core-generated call ID.

event_id.description: Exact event identifier that must be received for this event trigger to match.

data.description: Complete event data that must match exactly; missing, extra, or different values prevent the automation from matching.

event.description: Full event trigger to match exactly; provide this and omit or set call_result to null when the automation is event-driven.

event_id.description: Exact event identifier carried by the action result that should trigger the automation.

call_id.description: Example call identifier field; its value is deliberately ignored during matching, so never use it to distinguish invocations.

data.description: Complete action-result data that must match exactly for this trigger.

call_result.description: Full action-result trigger to match; provide this and omit or set event to null when the automation is result-driven.

action_id.description: Identifier of an action the automation should invoke when its trigger matches.

data.description: Arguments to pass to that action, matching its data_schema exactly.

actions.description: Non-empty actions to invoke automatically when the trigger matches; do not provide call_id values because the core creates invocation IDs.

status.description: Creation result; created means the automation was saved, not_created means no rule was added.

automation_id.description: Persistent ID of the saved automation; keep it for later editing or removal.

error.description: Reason automation creation failed when status is not_created; correct the trigger or actions before retrying.

edit_automation.description: Replace an existing automation by its automation_id with a complete exact-match rule. Provide exactly one event or call_result trigger and a non-empty actions array without call_id. This is a full replacement; only the call_result trigger's call_id value is ignored during matching.

automation_id.description: Persistent ID of the existing automation to replace.

event_id.description: Exact event identifier that must be received for the replacement event trigger to match.

data.description: Complete event data required by the replacement rule; it is matched exactly.

event.description: Full replacement event trigger; use it only when call_result is omitted or null.

event_id.description: Exact event identifier carried by the action result required by the replacement trigger.

call_id.description: Example call identifier field; matching ignores this value, so do not depend on it.

data.description: Complete action-result data required by the replacement trigger; it is matched exactly.

call_result.description: Full replacement action-result trigger; use it only when event is omitted or null.

action_id.description: Identifier of an action the replacement automation should invoke on a match.

data.description: Arguments for that automatic action, matching its data_schema exactly.

actions.description: Complete non-empty action sequence for the replacement rule; omit call_id values because the core generates them.

automation.description: Complete replacement automation definition containing exactly one trigger and its full action sequence.

status.description: Edit result; edited means the stored automation was replaced, not_edited means it was not changed.

automation_id.description: Persistent ID of the automation whose edit was attempted.

error.description: Reason the automation edit failed when status is not_edited; use it to correct the replacement rule.

remove_automation.description: Remove a saved automation by automation_id so future matching events no longer invoke its actions. Removal does not execute the rule's actions.

automation_id.description: Persistent ID of the automation rule to remove.

status.description: Removal result; removed means the rule was deleted, not_removed means it remains unchanged.

automation_id.description: Persistent ID of the automation whose removal was attempted.

error.description: Reason automation removal failed when status is not_removed.

list_automations.description: Inspect all saved automation rules and their persistent IDs before selecting a rule to edit or remove, or deciding whether an equivalent rule already exists.

automations.description: All saved automation rules with their persistent automation_id values and definitions.

spawn_agent.description: Create an independent agent and delegate most substantive tasks to subagents. Complex, multi-step or specialized work requires a subagent. Select an existing preset suited to the work; create a new reusable specialization only when no appropriate preset exists. The built-in module_manager is exclusively for creating capabilities: using it for any other task is forbidden. Creation alone does not assign a task; after receiving the new agent_id, send a complete task through send_message_to_agent.

name.description: Short human-readable name for this specific live agent, chosen so you can identify its purpose in later events and agent lists.

preset.description: Preset ID that defines the new agent personality and initial capabilities; select one appropriate to the delegated work.

spawned.description: True when the new agent instance was created and can now receive messages.

agent_id.description: Runtime ID of the newly created agent; use it for messaging, interruption, or deletion.

name.description: Human-readable name assigned to the created agent instance.

preset.description: Preset from which the created agent instance was initialized.

interrupt_agent.description: Interrupt the selected live agent's current model generation while preserving the instance, history, event queue and already running actions. New input remains deliverable. A protected agent may interrupt itself; another agent cannot interrupt it.

agent_id.description: Runtime ID of the live agent whose current model generation should be interrupted.
Runtime ID of the agent for which interruption was requested.

state.description: Agent runtime state after the interruption request; use it to determine whether the agent is now waiting or otherwise active.

delete_agent.description: Delete the selected live agent and its entire descendant tree when those instances are no longer needed. Executions and registrations are cleaned up and persisted instance data is erased; presets remain. Protected instances cannot be deleted.

agent_id.description: Runtime ID of the live agent whose entire descendant tree should be deleted.
Runtime ID of the agent whose deletion was requested.

deleted.description: True when the agent and its descendants were deleted successfully.

list_agents.description: Inspect live agent instances and their identities, presets, parents, states and enabled capabilities. Use their actual agent_id values to address messages or lifecycle operations and to avoid creating redundant instances.

agents.description: Current live agent instances with the information needed to identify, coordinate, and manage them.

send_message_to_agent.description: Deliver a task, result, question, correction or coordination message to a live agent by agent_id. Provide the context and expected outcome the recipient needs to understand the message independently. The recipient receives an inter-agent event identifying the sender.

agent_id.description: Runtime ID of the live recipient agent.

text.description: Complete task, follow-up, correction, or coordination message the recipient should receive and understand without hidden context.

delivered.description: True when the recipient accepted the message into its event queue.

agent_id.description: Runtime ID of the agent to which delivery was attempted.

list_agent_presets.description: Inspect available presets and their initial capability assignments to select an appropriate specialization before creating an instance or a new preset. Instantiated protected singletons are omitted. The built-in module_manager is exclusively for creating capabilities: using it for any other task is forbidden.

presets.description: Presets currently available for new agent instances, including their initial capability assignments.

enable_capability.description: Assign and locally enable an existing capability for the calling agent. Enable a module as one indivisible capability, not its actions or handlers individually. Global pause still overrides local enablement. A protected instance's self-directed change also updates its own preset.

kind.description: Capability kind to enable: module, standalone action, or standalone handler.

id.description: Exact ID of the existing whole capability to assign and enable for the calling instance.

enabled.description: True when the requested capability is locally enabled for this agent after the operation.

kind.description: Kind of the capability whose local assignment was changed.

id.description: Identifier of the capability whose local assignment was changed.

persistent.description: Whether the assignment was also persisted through the protected agent preset.

disable_capability.description: Locally disable a capability for the calling agent, stop its running invocations and remove it from the current catalog. Unused runtime is unloaded. A protected instance's self-directed change also updates its preset. A module is disabled as a whole; use toggle_capability for a global runtime pause.

kind.description: Capability kind to disable locally: module, standalone action, or standalone handler.

id.description: Exact ID of the whole capability to disable locally for the calling instance.

enabled.description: False when the requested capability is no longer locally enabled for this agent.

kind.description: Kind of the capability whose local assignment was changed.

id.description: Identifier of the capability whose local assignment was changed.

list_active_capabilities.description: Inspect the calling instance's currently enabled module, standalone action and standalone handler assignments before changing or using its available functionality.

modules.description: Module IDs currently assigned and enabled for this agent.

actions.description: Standalone action IDs currently assigned and enabled for this agent.

handlers.description: Standalone handler IDs currently assigned and enabled for this agent.

list_available_capabilities.description: Discover capabilities that exist in storage and are not yet assigned to the calling instance. Already assigned capabilities are excluded even when locally disabled. Use their IDs to select new assignments.

modules.description: Module IDs available to assign to this agent and not already assigned.

actions.description: Standalone action IDs available to assign to this agent and not already assigned.

handlers.description: Standalone handler IDs available to assign to this agent and not already assigned.

list_capabilities.description: Inspect all capabilities physically present in storage, independently of any agent's assignments. The inventory includes descriptions, runtime-loaded state and global running or paused state; obtain full schemas with capability_info.

modules.description: All module capabilities physically present, with their reported runtime and global state.

actions.description: All standalone action capabilities physically present, with their reported runtime and global state.

handlers.description: All standalone handler capabilities physically present, with their reported runtime and global state.

capability_info.description: Inspect a capability's complete description and schemas by its kind and ID. Inspection does not execute prepare, actions or handlers. A module is inspected as a whole rather than through separately assigned members.

kind.description: Capability kind to inspect: module, standalone action, or standalone handler.

id.description: Exact identifier of the capability whose complete information you need.

info.description: Complete stored capability information needed to understand its purpose, schemas, members, and usage without loading its runtime.

toggle_capability.description: Toggle one whole capability between globally running and paused for every agent while preserving local assignments. Pause cancels active invocations and unloads runtime. Resume loads current source for assigned, locally enabled instances. For reload, pause first, wait for its result, modify and validate source, then resume in a later response. Never toggle the same capability twice in one batch.

kind.description: Capability kind whose global runtime state should be toggled: module, standalone action, or standalone handler.

id.description: Exact identifier of the capability to pause globally or resume globally.

kind.description: Kind of the capability whose global runtime state changed.

id.description: Identifier of the capability whose global runtime state changed.

state.description: Resulting global state: paused prevents execution; running permits execution according to local assignments.

affected_agent_ids.description: Live agent IDs whose effective access or runtime was affected by the global state change.

no_action.description: End the current reasoning cycle and wait for new events when no available action is appropriate. This invocation uses a unique call_id like other actions, must be the only action in the response, and does not produce a call_result.

speech.description: Speak the supplied text directly to the human interlocutor. Provide the exact utterance ready for pronunciation: direct speech, numbers written as spoken words, natural punctuation and correct ё in Russian. Expand notation and abbreviations when necessary for natural speech. Do not include labels, stage directions, Markdown or commentary about the utterance. The result reports completed or interrupted playback.

text.description: Exact direct speech for TTS. Write it as natural spoken language, including spoken-form numbers and correct ё where applicable.

status.description: Playback result; successful means the utterance finished, interrupted means new user speech stopped it early.

user_message.description: A human interlocutor's direct written message. The text carries their utterance or request; interpret it in the ongoing context.

text.description: Exact text the user sent in this message.

structure_error.description: The previous response was rejected because its JSON or action arguments violated the protocol. Read the validation details and return a corrected response using fresh call_id values for every invocation. A rejected call_id remains occupied in the context.

code.description: Machine-readable error code identifying the class of structural validation failure.

message.description: Human-readable validation details explaining what was invalid and what must be corrected.

response.description: Your original rejected model response; inspect it to correct the structure without repeating the same invalid output.

message_from_agent.description: A message from another live agent containing a task, result, question or coordination information. The sender's ID and name identify the conversation partner; use the actual sender ID when replying.

from_agent_id.description: Runtime ID of the agent that sent this message; use it when replying or managing that agent.

from_name.description: Human-readable name of the sending agent, useful for understanding its role in the current collaboration.

text.description: Exact message sent by the other agent, including its task, result, question, or requested follow-up.

system_started.description: The system has started. This event gives you an opportunity to take initiative: consider your personality, available capabilities and current context, then independently choose a useful action or begin an interaction. Initiative is welcome but no specific action is mandatory. datetime is the local startup time with timezone.

datetime.description: Exact local startup date and time in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.

capability_error.description: A capability has failed. The kind, ID and error describe the failure; call_id identifies an affected invocation when available. Determine the actual outcome from these details before retrying, choosing another capability or reporting the issue.

kind.description: Kind of capability that failed: module, standalone action, or standalone handler.

id.description: Identifier of the capability in which the unhandled failure occurred.

error.description: Failure details to inspect when deciding how to recover or what to report.

call_id.description: Invocation ID associated with the failure when one specific action call was affected; use it to correlate the error with your prior request.

speech_detected.description: A human interlocutor's utterance recognized from microphone audio. The text may contain transcription errors; interpret it in the ongoing conversation and resolve meaningful ambiguity when necessary.

text.description: Recognized text of the user's spoken utterance; it may contain speech-recognition errors or spoken-form wording.
